overview.title: How CFN turns work into checked results
overview.summary: A plan travels as two artifacts: the PLAN file and the VERIFY manifest (the final fenced JSON block of the VERIFY markdown). Before implementation the pair must clear two static gates: Bar A (check-verifiable-static.sh) machine-checks the manifest for decidable pass predicates, a closed kind vocabulary, paired coverage counters and executed evidence (PENDING tolerated only at plan stage), while Bar B (check-haiku-static.sh) scans the PLAN itself for banned vague phrases; only bless-verify.sh may pin a cleared manifest, producing the sha256 sidecar (.VERIFY_<slug>.sha256), a .blessed.json snapshot and the append-only .bless.json ledger that cfn-loop-task Step 0 and verify-run.sh consume (a mismatched sidecar makes verify-run exit 4). Implementation then runs as an orchestration loop over a task's declared deliverables: Loop 3 spawns implementers and waits on file-based done markers, executeTestsOnDeliverables existence-checks each deliverable and runs the allowlisted TEST_COMMAND parsing Jest-format summaries, the pass-rate gate decides the Loop 3 to Loop 2 transition, Loop 2 validators score confidence against a consensus threshold, and the product-owner script returns PROCEED, ITERATE or ABORT (an errored or unparseable PO run defaults to PROCEED). Completion is proven separately by the task exit workflow: verify-run.sh re-reads the manifest (sidecar checked when present), executes each runnable acceptance criterion under a timeout, adjudicates captured stdout through the shared parse-test-summary.sh (zero collected tests is red; an unrecognized summary degrades to exit-code-only, and a non-asserting exit 0 stays predicate_unverified), and writes VERIFY_RESULTS rows plus the all_green summary (total>0, red=0, unresolved=0) that the remaining exit gates build on: evidence resolve, exit-stage re-bless where surviving PENDING becomes a hard error, a full-suite final gate and deferral checks. Two gaps survive the accepted sources: no shard establishes who invokes the bar checkers inside megaplan or which step blocks implementation start (enforcement references appear only in comments of the scope files), and the loop-orchestration walkthrough never mentions the sidecar or manifest, so the handoff from the blessed VERIFY into the orchestration loop is unproven; additionally no process exit code reflects the PO decision, because the CLI tail never calls execute() and an undecided run reads as ABORT. Landing a fleet worker's done claim runs two chains the accepted sources never connect. Claims come first: fleet claim appends the worker's paths to its roster row under the flock (refusing overlap with any other row, exit 65), and that claims column is exactly what the later dirty-file gate tests against. The worker-side chain proves the work: verify-run.sh re-reads the VERIFY manifest (a mismatched integrity sidecar exits 4), executes each acceptance criterion, writes VERIFY_RESULTS rows plus the all_green summary (total>0, red=0, unresolved=0), routes unresolved criteria to evidence resolve (existing AC id, true/false verdict, at least three evidence lines) with red or unresolved sending the task back to its bounded iteration loop, and only then applies the remaining exit gates (evidence backfill, re-bless, full-suite final gate, deferral checks). The master-side land gate is git-state hygiene only: main mode exits 66 listing any unclaimed dirty file outside the run dir, worktree mode exits 66 on an uncommitted worktree before merging fleet/<WSxx> ff-only and removing it, and success stamps status=landed plus landed_sha through roster_set and best-effort echoes residual handoffs. Neither shard shows cmd-land reading VERIFY_RESULTS or all_green, so whether completion proof gates landing at all is open; equally open is the roster bridge, since no status between started and landed is established and nothing in either shard says what marks a worker done or triggers the land call. Runtime state lands in three separate stores: agent output is written to a SQLite memory_store table by persist-agent-output.sh (inline SQLiteAdapter.set under key agent/<id>/output/<task>) with ttl-cleanup.sh expiring rows per ACL retention tier and reconciling Redis memory:* keys; curated decisions and raw conversation go to one SQLite DB at ~/.claude/decision-log/decisions.db (decisions upserted by record.sh, messages mirrored into FTS5 for BM25 search by query.sh); and live loop state rides Redis keys swarm:<taskId>:* which the portal's CFNMetricsClient reads. Browsers read state back through two servers: the portal API exposes /api/events queries, /api/agents hierarchy/status reads served from transparencyService, and metrics plus pSubscribe-driven WebSocket push from those swarm:<taskId>:* keys, while the monitoring dashboard's Express server (port 5555) is polled by dashboard.html every 10 s across /api/containers, /api/system, /api/cfn (Redis cfn_loop:*:context: keys), /api/agents (SELECT * FROM agents in ../claude-assets/skills/cfn-redis-coordination/data/cfn-loop.db) and /api/redis/signals (swarm:* keys). The shards do not connect these stores: portal-api reading agent-memory's SQLite is established in neither shard (the /api/events persistence backend eventStoreController is unverified), the monitoring dashboard reads a third SQLite DB (cfn-loop.db) distinct from both the memory_store database and decisions.db, and decisions.db has no browser reader at all since query.sh is CLI-only and the curated-decisions reader decisions.sh is named only in a schema comment. Loop status also arrives under two different Redis key families, swarm:<taskId>:status for the portal metrics client versus cfn_loop:*:context: for monitoring's /api/cfn, and neither shard establishes who writes either family. Consistency across sharing projects rests on three mechanisms the shards name: the skill pipeline gates every update twice (review-skill.sh flips a Postgres workflow_patterns row to APPROVED in one transaction, then propagate-skill-update.sh or its SkillPropagator twin re-registers the update in the SQLite skills registry, refusing unchanged versions, downgrades, change-type mismatches and sha256-identical content); the edit-safety hooks fire on edit and spawn from the shared tree (the post-edit wrapper resolves its pipeline path against the real repo root via pwd -P so invocation through the ~/.claude symlink works, with pre-edit backups, the doc-lint gate and the spawn depth guard carrying the block semantics); and generated docs are held consistent by sync.sh's deterministic no-LLM regeneration plus its --check drift gate, which exits 1 WIKI STALE on a missing or mismatched wiki-fp fingerprint marker, while sha256-grounded claims are flagged needs_review on hash mismatch and work.py refuses submissions planned at an older revision. The drift gaps are structural: skill review (Postgres) and propagation (SQLite registry) are decoupled, with the bridge between them outside the scoped files, and neither stage copies content anywhere (notify_affected_agents only lists affected agents in the log), so the physical distribution layer, the reverse-symlinked ~/.claude dirs named only in repo docs, is unverified. Likewise the hook registration surface (settings.json) sits outside the index, so whether the guards are registered at all, and whether .claude/hooks.json has any consumer, is unknown; and the guards default to non-blocking (post-edit exits 0 unless --blocking, doc-lint escalates to exit 2 only under CFN_DOC_LINT_BLOCK=1), so a skipped or unregistered guard lets drift pass silently. Consistency is thus established piecewise, per-pipeline validation, per-edit hooks and per-regeneration drift checks, but not end-to-end. Containerized teams are provisioned by docker/scripts/provision-team.sh, which turns a team YAML into an isolated enclave in flag-gated idempotent steps: workspace directories with a copy of only the allowed skills, a bridge network team-<id> on 172.18.<subnet>.0/24, a team Redis pinned to .20 with a persistent volume, a teams-table row via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and a coordinator container that receives /var/run/docker.sock and is then attached to the team network, with DOCKER-USER iptables rules letting agents reach only their coordinator (.10) and Redis (.20). Database access is scoped by Postgres user, not by network: docker/skills/database-readonly/query.sh connects to cfn-postgres as readonly_user and pre-blocks writes with a case-insensitive substring denylist (INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|DROP|CREATE|ALTER|TRUNCATE) before psql runs, an application-level check that also refuses read queries merely naming a column like created_at and is not evidence of a DB-enforced permission, while docker/skills/database-readwrite/migrate.sh connects as admin_user but is a declared placeholder whose migration-tool integration is a Phase-2 TODO. Coordination inside containers rides Redis and Postgres (per-team Redis, the main coordinator subscribing to main:escalations and polling team:*:coordinator:heartbeat into main:health), a separate plane from the fleet's file-based TSV roster with its flock-serialized claims, spawn banner gate, and land dirty-file gate; neither shard establishes any bridge between the two, so whether a containerized team ever appears as a roster row or shares the claims/land discipline is open. Teardown is absent from the sources: agent-manager.js spawn/terminate/monitor/recover are empty Phase-2 stubs and provision-team.sh has no decommission mode, so containers, the team network, and the cfn-redis-<id>-data volume persist until removed by hand, and where readonly_user and admin_user are provisioned (init SQL, compose env, or GRANTs) is likewise unverified.
overview.coverage: One capability has been traced in depth. The remaining directory entries are an inventory and have not been reviewed as independent capabilities.
questions: How does a caller learn the orchestrator's final decision, given no process exit code reflects PROCEED, ITERATE or ABORT?
Who invokes the megaplan bar checkers, and at which exact step does a failed gate block implementation from starting?
Does the orchestration loop consume the blessed VERIFY sidecar, or are the deliverable-plus-TEST_COMMAND gate and the verify-run.sh manifest path two separate verification entries?
Does fleet land ever consume the worker's VERIFY_RESULTS or all_green verdict, or is task-completion proof entirely disjoint from the landing gate?
What roster status (if any) marks a fleet worker done between started and landed, and what triggers the master to invoke fleet land?
Does the portal's /api/events backend (eventStoreController) read or write the same SQLite memory_store that persist-agent-output.sh writes, or are events and agent memory entirely disjoint stores?

Who writes the swarm:<taskId>:* and cfn_loop:* Redis key families that the portal metrics client and monitoring /api/cfn consume, and is loop status duplicated across both families or produced by different components?

Does any component bridge the Postgres APPROVED state to the SQLite skills registry that propagate reads (the sibling deploy-approved-skill.sh?), and does any code copy skill content to sharing projects, or is the reverse-symlinked ~/.claude layout the only distribution layer, unverified by every shard?

Where do the edit-safety guards actually register, given the registration records sit outside the index and .claude/hooks.json may have zero consumers, and since the post-edit pipeline exits 0 unless --blocking and doc-lint exits 2 only under CFN_DOC_LINT_BLOCK=1, is any consistency guard blocking by default anywhere?

Is a containerized team ever represented in the fleet roster's TSV (a row, claims, or the land gate), or are the Redis/Postgres container coordination and the file-based fleet roster two disjoint coordination planes with no shared component?

Where are readonly_user and admin_user provisioned (init SQL, compose env, or GRANT statements), and does Postgres itself restrict readonly_user to SELECT, given the query.sh denylist is the only access control the shard could see?
